piezas.titulo: Reading words: Greetings and polite phrases
texto: When reading polite phrases, look at the consonant and vowel spelling: «สวัสดี» is made of ส (high class), ว (low class) and the group สด, which makes the short closed syllable «sàt», ending with the long vowel ี (dii). In «ขอบคุณ», ข is a high-class consonant with an implicit, closed short vowel, and คุณ gives the mid tone. In «ขอโทษ», ษ works as a final consonant with the sound [t]. Recognising these spellings lets you read welcome signs and everyday notes accurately.

pregunta.texto: Reading comprehension: According to the text, which idea does the sentence «คำลงท้ายช่วยปรับระดับความสุภาพให้เหมาะกับสถานการณ์และผู้ฟัง» express?

opciones.texto: Final particles adjust the level of politeness to the situation and the listener.
opciones.explicacion: Correct: this option translates and accurately interprets the sentence «คำลงท้ายช่วยปรับระดับความสุภาพให้เหมาะกับสถานการณ์และผู้ฟัง» from the text.

opciones.texto: Saying thank you and apologising regularly creates a good atmosphere for conversation.
opciones.explicacion: Incorrect: this is another statement from the text, not the meaning of the sentence in question.

opciones.texto: The wai, said with «sawàtdii», is a traditional sign of respect.
opciones.explicacion: Incorrect: this option corresponds to another sentence in the reading passage.

pregunta.texto: In the word «ขอโทษ» (sorry), which final letter represents the stop sound [t]?

opciones.texto: ษ (in the syllable โทษ)
opciones.explicacion: Correct: ษ belongs to the high class, and at the end of a syllable it sounds like [t] (section แม่กด).
ข is the initial consonant of the first syllable, not the final consonant.
ท is the initial consonant of the second syllable, before ษ.
